author: human
request:
Bug report: opening /owners?page=0 — or any page value below 1 — renders the
error page instead of the owner list. Expected behavior: the owner listing
treats any page value below 1 as the first page and responds with the normal
listing (HTTP 200). Find the cause, fix it, and cover the fix with a test.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Owner listing shows the first page when a page before the first is asked for
summary: Asking the owner listing for a page before the first shows the first page of owners and the normal listing, rather than an error page.
acceptance_criteria: given the owner list, when a page before the first is asked for, then the first page of owners is shown
given the owner list, when a page before the first is asked for, then the reader is shown the normal listing rather than an error page
given a zero page and given a negative page, when either is asked for, then both show the first page
given a search result listing and given the full list of owners, when a page before the first is asked for, then both behave the same
non_goals: behavior for a page past the last page
behavior for a page value that is not a number
the veterinarian directory listing, which is unexamined
notes: Bug fix slice: the listing currently renders the error page for a page below the first. PRD edits: REQ-OWN-005 narrative, anchor, two Done-when bullets, edge cases 4 and 5 under Owner records, one new Open Question, and a provenance note marking REQ-OWN-005 as owner-stated rather than derived. No Non-Goals row changed. No ubiquitous-language entry added: the PRD already uses 'a page at a time' in REQ-OWN-002 and REQ-VET-001, so the requirement needed no new domain term. The owner recorded no decisions beyond the quoted bug report, so the two neighboring cases stay open rather than being scoped in by default. REQ-SYS-002 is unaffected: the error page stays correct for genuine failures.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The slice is boundary input normalization on an existing seam, not new design ground. system-design.md #contracts already names OwnerController as the owner of server-rendered owner workflows including search with paging; the paging helper it owns is the whole surface. The defect is that the request-supplied page reaches PageRequest.of unnormalized (OwnerController.java:135, findPaginatedForOwnersLastName), which rejects a zero-based index below zero and lets the resulting IllegalArgumentException reach the error page. Normalizing the page to the first page at the controller is exactly the security-principles.md #trust-boundaries first row: validate range at the point external input arrives. It is also squarely inside the architecture-principles.md Web controller row, which owns request binding; page indexing is a presentation concern and not a domain rule, so the clamp is NOT a fresh instance of the controllers-carry-rules deviation that row records. No new type, package, dependency, or pattern. Verified by grep on OwnerController.java and VetController.java; the IDE oracle is not connected in this run, so the resolution basis is the weaker one. The only durable-memory write is REQ-OWN-005 joining the OwnerController Contracts row, plus one clause on that row's purpose naming the guarantee.
integration_points: Repository boundary: OwnerRepository. The double is the @MockitoBean OwnerRepository already declared on OwnerControllerTests (line 70) and stubbed with PageImpl throughout the class. Reuse that existing collaborator; introduce no new stub. Testing-principles tolerates the established Mockito seam here, and a hand-written repository double inside a @WebMvcTest slice would be a novel shape for one test.

Framework transport boundary: Spring MockMvc under @WebMvcTest(OwnerController.class). MockMvc is the one sanctioned mock per CLAUDE.md; it drives the real dispatch, binding, and view resolution, which is what makes the HTTP 200 and view-name assertions meaningful.
No new route, model attribute, template, or repository method. owners/ownersList and the existing currentPage, totalPages, totalItems, listOwners model attributes are unchanged.

patterns.description: processFindForm is the single entry point for both the empty-search full listing and the last-name search; both reach the page value through the same helper, so one normalization at entry satisfies the PRD's search-and-full-list parity criterion without a second code path

testProcessFindFormSuccess is the adjacent test shape to copy: stub findByLastNameStartingWith with a PageImpl, perform get("/owners?page=..."), assert status().isOk() and view().name("owners/ownersList")

risks.risk: Normalizing inside findPaginatedForOwnersLastName only. The repository would then receive the first page while addPaginationModel still puts the raw request value into the currentPage model attribute, so the page renders first-page rows labelled page 0 or page -3. That splits the two Done-when bullets: the first page is shown, but the listing the reader sees is not the normal one.
risks.mitigation: Normalize once at the top of processFindForm, before the value reaches either the repository call or addPaginationModel, so both read the same normalized value (architecture-principles.md Web controller row: bind the request, then delegate).

risks.risk: Asserting only status().isOk() would pass against a controller that swallows the page value entirely, so the test would not pin the first-page behavior the requirement states.
risks.mitigation: Assert the observable first-page outcome too: capture the Pageable passed to findByLastNameStartingWith and assert its page number is the first, and assert the currentPage model attribute is 1 (testing-principles.md assertion patterns).

risks.risk: VetController.java:61 carries the identical PageRequest.of(page - 1, pageSize) expression and the same defect. The PRD lists the veterinarian directory as a non-goal for this slice, and system-design.md #constants records that the two pagination helpers are declared independently.
risks.mitigation: Change OwnerController only. Do not extract a shared helper, a shared constant, or a base class in this slice; the divergence is the product expert's open question, not this slice's to settle.

risks.risk: Scope creep into the two neighboring cases the PRD explicitly excludes: a page past the last page, and a non-numeric page value. The latter fails during request binding before the handler body runs, so a normalization written to cover it would need a binding or exception-handling change well outside this slice.
risks.mitigation: Handle values below the first page only. Leave the binding behavior and the past-the-end behavior exactly as they are.

notes: Five-signal foundational check: none trips. system-design.md, the ADR set, and ubiquitous-language.md are all populated and confirmed; the slice introduces no bounded context and touches no project-level concern lacking a recorded pattern. No ADR is warranted — the choice carries no trade-off a later slice must not re-open, so the rationale is one clause on the Contracts row. No ubiquitous-language change: 'a page at a time' is already the PRD's phrasing and the slice introduces no domain term. No Known Defects row is added; the defect is fixed inside this slice, and that table records current state. Secondary benefit worth knowing but not worth designing for: the fix removes one path on which an internal exception message reaches the error page, which system-design.md #known-defects records as breaching REQ-SYS-002. That defect itself is untouched and out of scope. Autofix audit: the handoff log contains no design-doc-autofix records, so nothing to audit.

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: Supply chain was NOT verified against the NVD in this review: no OWASP dependency-check plugin is configured in build.gradle (plugins are java, checkstyle, jacoco, spring-boot 4.1.1, dependency-management, graalvm native, cyclonedx, javaformat, nohttp), so no CVE match ran. The slice changes no dependency, so this is a standing gap for CI or a human to close, not a defect of this change.

Divergence worth tracking, not blocking: VetController.showVetList (src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/vet/VetController.java:45,61) keeps the unclamped @RequestParam(defaultValue = "1") int page feeding PageRequest.of(page - 1, ...), so page=0 there still throws IllegalArgumentException into the error page that renders the exception message. Pre-existing and explicitly scoped out by the new PRD open question, so it is not a finding against this change; the same clamp applied there would remove the last instance of the class.

A page past the last one and a non-numeric page remain unhandled for owners as well (the latter surfaces a MethodArgumentTypeMismatch through the detail-rendering error page). Both are pre-existing baseline behavior recorded as the PRD's new open question.
approved_aspects: Boundary validation strengthened, not weakened: the clamp normalizes a request-supplied page at the controller trust boundary per security-principles.md#trust-boundaries. Math.max(page, FIRST_PAGE) has no overflow edge (page=Integer.MIN_VALUE clamps to 1), and it removes the pre-existing integer-underflow path where page-1 wrapped to Integer.MAX_VALUE inside findPaginatedForOwnersLastName.

No injection surface: paging still flows through PageRequest.of into the derived repository query findByLastNameStartingWith; no query text is concatenated and no request-derived value composes a path or resource name.

No output-escaping change: the only new model value is the int currentPage; no template was touched, Thymeleaf default escaping is untouched, and there is no th:utext or __${...} preprocessing anywhere in src/main/resources/templates.

No new dependency, no build.gradle change, and no credential-shaped literal in the diff (grep of the change set for token/password/secret/key returns nothing). Supply-chain surface is unchanged by this slice.
No new endpoint, no widened management exposure, no serialization, no file or process I/O, no logging added; the controller stays stateless, so the singleton bean gains no mutable shared state.
Test additions use MockMvc against the real MVC binding path and assert the Pageable actually handed to the repository, which pins the clamp at the boundary rather than at an internal seam.

author: test-reviewer
approved_aspects: Placement is correct: system-design.md#contracts assigns the page-clamp as an OwnerController (boundary) rule, and both new tests exercise it at the @WebMvcTest web layer via MockMvc rather than extracting it into a unit — matches testing-principles.md's pyramid placement rule.

Full PRD coverage per coverage-map: both REQ-OWN-005 Done-when bullets are named by theOwnerListingShouldShowTheFirstPageWhenAPageBeforeTheFirstIsRequested, and edge cases 4 (zero and negative page via @ParameterizedTest @ValueSource(ints={0,-3})) and 5 (search-vs-full-list parity via the paired theOwnerSearchShouldShowTheFirstPageWhenAPageBeforeTheFirstIsRequested test) are both exercised.

Mocking stays within the design-block's sanctioned seam: the pre-existing @MockitoBean OwnerRepository and MockMvc; no new stub framework introduced. The ArgumentCaptor+verify on Pageable is not a redundant restatement of the currentPage model assertion - the repository stub returns fixed data regardless of the Pageable argument, so the captor is the only check that pins the clamped value at the query boundary, guarding exactly the split-normalization regression the design-block's risk section called out.

Test data naming follows the three-tier convention (FIRST_PAGE_NUMBER, FIRST_PAGE_INDEX derived from it, NO_LAST_NAME_FILTER, SOME_LAST_NAME) and adds anOwner()/aPageOfSeveralOwners() factories consistent with the suite's existing bare-name factory idiom (george()).
BDD test naming (the{Subject}Should{Outcome}) matches testing-principles.md's naming school and the PRD's recorded test_names field exactly.
Four-phase structure held (arrange via when(...), act+assert via the MockMvc chain, blank line, second assertThat assertion); no phase-comment narration in the new tests.

Full ./gradlew test suite passes; conventions-map's flagged literal-bearing lines are all framework-idiom strings (URL path, view name, model attribute key) inherent to the existing MockMvc convention, not mystery test-data values.

author: change-grader
summary: clamp owner-listing page below the first to the first page

blast_radius.note: One module and one production method: 10 added prod lines across 2 hunks in OwnerController.processFindForm, no sensitive paths, no new route, model attribute, template, or repository method; the other two changed files are docs, and the identical unclamped path in VetController is deliberately left untouched.

semantic_surprise.note: Reading the hunk, Math.max(page, FIRST_PAGE) is the identity for every page at or above 1, so no existing positive-page behavior shifts; the clamped value is computed once and threaded to both findPaginatedForOwnersLastName and addPaginationModel, no use of the raw page parameter survives, and Integer.MIN_VALUE clamps cleanly rather than underflowing through page - 1.

test_adequacy.note: The two new parameterized tests are real rather than tautological - they drive the real MVC binding through MockMvc, fail against the pre-fix code, and pin both the Pageable index handed to the repository and the currentPage model attribute, so neither half of a split normalization could pass - but every other page assertion in the suite uses page=1, so nothing anywhere exercises a page above the first; an implementation that hard-pinned the listing to the first page would pass the whole suite green.

reviewer_hedging.note: All four planned reviewers approved with zero findings; the security reviewer's three recommendations are explicitly pre-existing and out of scope (no NVD plugin configured, the unclamped VetController page, page-past-last and non-numeric page), all already parked in the PRD's new open question, so they are context rather than reservation - though one of its approved_aspects claims no Thymeleaf preprocessing expressions exist under templates, which ownersList.html lines 44, 49 and 54 contradict; the values there are ints and the template is untouched, so the claim is inaccurate rather than the escaping unsafe.

scope_deviation.note: Zero design revisions, zero consultations, zero build retries, and the diff lands exactly on the design-block's primary paths plus the PRD entry the earlier hop authored; the change adds one requirement and one clamp and explicitly declines to generalize to the veterinarian listing, recording that as an open question instead.

rationale: The clamp itself reads clean and changes nothing for pages at or above the first. Read the one production hunk plus the new tests to confirm you are comfortable that no test anywhere covers a page above the first - a first-page-always regression would ship green.
